findings.title: Two-player 'Break the ground' (Collide, Rex bolted): the box names the effort that breaks the ground, then says nothing in the test does harm even all-out. The real-ground ceiling ignores both the broken rock and the hit's shaking
findings.location: src/app.html duoFacts (collide branch, about line 3765-3771: out.harm never tests out.ground; the shaking check uses r.toGround only); resolveDuoEffort 'least:real' job; src/engine.js collide() line 2189 (toGround only when cA.unbreakable || cB.unbreakable)
findings.evidence: State {duoOpen:true, duoAction:'collide', anchor:'bolted'} at the default dial, Rex + Ollie effort 'Break the ground under him'. The page says: 'Rock cracks 5.1 cm around his bolts' / 'Effort: 4.1% of their strength (each as hard as lifting 3.69 t). The least effort that breaks the ground under their feet.' / 'Unbreakable footing is set aside for this test…' / 'On real ground, courtesy ceiling: none. Nothing in this test does harm, even all-out, with the nearest people and buildings 5 m away.' (The same at logKg 7.) Same settings with the power on and Least disruptive: 'Courtesy ceiling: 8.7% (lifting 7.86 t). Past that, the hit, carried into the unbreakable ground, shakes it enough that plaster may crack 5 m away.' Engine (scratch e8.js): at 7.86 t the held hit gives the planet h.inel.pT = 4.32e4 kg·m/s whether or not the power is on, but with unbreakable false collide() returns toGround undefined, so the real-ground run has no shaking. The rock cracks from 3.69 t (rock.rT 0.051 m), and duoFacts' Collide harm never counts out.ground. The solo tabs count both on real ground: Stomp with 'Break the ground' says 'Courtesy ceiling: 5.6% (lifting 5.08 t). Past that, the ground under his feet gives way.'
findings.expected: Brief 5c says to offer the presets 'as the solo tabs do', and that the same push shakes the ground 'exactly as real physics says'. On real ground the courtesy ceiling here should stop at the first harm: the rock cracking (about 3.7 t), and in any case no later than the plaster onset of the same hit (about 7.9 t). It must not call an effort harmless when the same box says that effort breaks the ground.
findings.fix: In duoFacts, add a broken-ground harm wherever out.ground is set (Collide, and Catch's catcher's feet), skipped only when P.holdsGround applies, for example `: out.ground ? 'the ground breaks under ' + Y : slides(slid)`. For the 'real' variant, keep the hit's push into the ground: compute it on the page from r.h (held: splat ? h.inel.pT : h.el.pT over the contact time; knocked back: r.partial.Jearth over r.partial.tau) when Unbreakable footing is only set aside, or pass the engine a flag that returns toGround without holding the ground.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced on the built page (dist matches a fresh build of the sources). With Rex bolted on Collide, the 'Break the ground' preset (run on real ground) finds 4.1% because duoFacts sets out.ground once rock.rT >= 0.05 m. The real-ground ceiling ('least:real') then says no effort does harm. That ceiling job runs duoFacts with {unbreakable:false}, and in that run two things are missing. First, collide() returns no toGround, because the engine gates it at line 2189 on cA.unbreakable || cB.unbreakable. Second, the Collide harm line (app.html 3771) never tests out.ground. The same hit still hands the planet the same momentum on real ground (pT 4.81e4 kg·m/s at 9 t, either way). The lab's own impulseSource says that shaking cracks plaster at 5 m from about 9 t, and the power-on ceiling says 8.7%. So the sentence 'Nothing in this test does harm, even all-out' is false, and it contradicts the line just above it ('The least effort that breaks the ground'). Decisions 2 and 13 explain why a real-ground ceiling exists and why shaking is off when the powers are off. Neither makes the ceiling free to ignore the break it reports, or to claim no harm without saying the shaking isn't judged. On main, Collide's harm also skipped the cracked rock, but the preset and the real-ground ceiling are new in this branch. The solo Stomp preset does this correctly: 'Courtesy ceiling: 5.6% (lifting 5.08 t). Past that, the ground under his feet gives way.'

findings.title: They take their own recoil on Pull sends the rope's pull back into the planet, but its ground shaking is never judged, and no recorded decision covers this
findings.location: src/engine.js RESTRAINT.MOVES.pull (no shake); pull() with ctx.ownRecoil; src/app.html bayPull
findings.evidence: Brief 5d lists 'a pull' and says the effort and presets judge that push into the ground 'as for any other push into the ground'. With the default powers the Pull tab reads 'Courtesy ceiling: none… It doesn’t model the ground shaking from this move.' Engine (scratch e6.js), Boeing 777 at a 1e9 kg dial on concrete. With the power on: accel 5.88 m/s², 10 m in 1.84 s, so the planet takes J = 2.68e6 kg·m/s over 1.84 s. The lab's own impulseSource gives 2.37 mm/s at 2 m and 1.58 mm/s at 3 m (past the 1 mm/s rattle line) and 4.74 mm/s at 1 m (plaster). With the power off it is 2.84e5 kg·m/s over 17.4 s, about 1,000× less shaking. The power raises this push tenfold, but with the nearest people set to 3 m or less the page can't show any rattle or plaster from it.
findings.expected: Either the pull's push into the planet goes through the same ground-wave model as the throw and punch (impulseSource of the load's momentum over the pull time, with ownRecoil or unbreakable on), or a recorded decision says why it is left out (a slow pull spread over seconds) and the page gives that reason.
findings.fix: Add MOVES.pull.shake = (r, o) => (o.ownRecoil && r.canMove ? impulseSource(o.surface, vToMomentum(r.vEnd, o.obj.m) + r.resist * r.t10m, r.t10m) : null) with shakeWithPower, or record the decision in the README and the page.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced. MOVES.pull has no shake, so with They take their own recoil on, the rope's pull back that goes into the planet is never judged. Brief 5d lists 'a pull' and says 'the effort and presets judge that shaking as for any other push into the ground'. The power raises this push about 10× (2.68e6 vs 3.05e5 kg·m/s for the 777) and shortens it about 10× (1.84 s vs 17.4 s). Fed through the lab's own impulseSource, the shaking reaches rattle level inside about 4.7 m and plaster level at 1 m. The page and the README Known limits ('Ground shaking is not modelled for Sprint, Pull or Clap … and the page says so') label the gap honestly, so the finding's 'no recorded decision' overstates it. But neither says why the gap is acceptable with the power on, as brief 5c asks ('say why there is none'). The practical effect is small: the 777 is the heaviest pullable object, and its maximum (load accel capped at about 5.9 m/s² by his footing) stays under the 1 mm/s rattle line at the default 5 m (0.95 mm/s). It only matters when the nearest-people distance is set below about 4.7 m.

Nothing the lab checks for this move harms anyone 2 m or more away, even all-out. It doesn’t model the ground shaking from this move.' The lab's own model gives 2.37 mm/s at 2 m, past the 1 mm/s rattle line. With effort 'rattle' the page says it can't judge rattle through the ground.
verdict.better_fix: In engine RESTRAINT.MOVES.pull add `shake: (r, o) => (o.ownRecoil && o.anchor !== 'bolted' && r.canMove && isFinite(r.t10m) ? impulseSource(o.surface, vToMomentum(r.vEnd, o.obj.m) + r.resist * r.t10m, r.t10m) : null)`. findings.evidence: Throw, baseball, logKg 15, 45°, air 92%, all-out: 'At 632 km/s it is far past the 11.2 km/s …, the 42.1 km/s …, and the 445 km/s–580 km/s that published estimates give for leaving the Milky Way from the Sun’s position: it leaves the galaxy too'. The research note for milky_way_escape_speed_solar says: 'the speed is relative to the Galaxy’s centre … a throw … straight against [the Sun's orbit] roughly 765 km/s'. The solar branch handles direction (the 71.9 km/s threshold); the galaxy branch doesn't.
findings.expected: Between about 445 and roughly 820 km/s (580 + the Sun's 230–240 km/s), whether it leaves the galaxy depends on the direction. And 632 km/s isn't 'far past' 580.
findings.fix: Use u >= es.galaxyHi + (Sun's circular speed, about 240 km/s, from the same fact's notes) for 'leaves the galaxy in any direction'. Between galaxyLo and that, say it depends on the way it goes. Drop 'far'.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced. The u >= es.galaxyHi branch says that at 632 km/s it is 'far past' the 445-580 km/s range and 'leaves the galaxy too'. The fact's own research note (milky_way_escape_speed_solar) says the speed is relative to the Galaxy's centre: a throw along the Sun's orbit needs roughly 300 km/s and one straight against it roughly 765 km/s. At the 580 km/s high estimate, against the Sun's motion needs about 580 + 235 = 815 km/s. So at 632 km/s the outcome depends on direction, and 632 is not 'far past' 580. The solar-system branch already handles direction; the galaxy branch does not.
verdict.reproduction: node page.js branch '{"state":{"action":"throw","obj":"baseball","logKg":15,"angle":45,"airAbsorb":0.92},"effort":"allout"}' -> 'At 632 km/s it is far past the 11.2 km/s needed to escape the Earth, the 42.1 km/s ..., and the 445 km/s–580 km/s that published estimates give for leaving the Milky Way from the Sun's position: it leaves the galaxy too'. research/final-environment.json notes: 'the speed is relative to the Galaxy's centre ... a throw along the Sun's orbit needs roughly 300 km/s relative to the Sun, and one straight against it roughly 765 km/s ... These are rough figures, not sourced.' Code app.html:1336 tests only u >= es.galaxyHi.
verdict.better_fix: In away(u): const vSun = 235e3 (from the fact's notes; label it rough). u >= es.galaxyHi + vSun -> 'it leaves the galaxy whichever way it goes'. u >= es.galaxyLo - vSun -> 'whether it also leaves the galaxy depends on the way it goes (the published 445–580 km/s is measured from the Galaxy's centre, and the Sun circles it at roughly 230–240 km/s)'. Drop 'far'.

findings.outcome: fixed with air-away-galaxy

findings.title: Throw item says the air takes more energy than the object had (8.35 MJ of 8.32 MJ)
findings.location: src/engine.js:478-491 (tally uses the drag at each step's start: a left sum); src/app.html:1486 (prints f.air.E)
findings.evidence: Throw, baseball, logKg 9, level, Air resistance absorbed 30%, effort 'windows'. Tile: 'Energy in the baseball 8.32 MJ'. Item: '…and the air takes the rest: 8.35 MJ over its flight'. Engine at use 2.3e8 kg: Eobj 8.3407e6 J, flight.air.E 8.3639e6 J, landing 1.9 kJ, dragLoss (energy balance) 8.3389e6 J. findings.fix: Print (1 − share)-scaled energy from the flight's energy balance (r.dragLoss is already that for the slowed flight), or integrate the tally with the step's mean drag (trapezoid) so it stays within the energy balance.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced. The new flight tally (engine ~478-491) is a left Riemann sum: each step uses the drag at its start, which overstates the work while drag is falling. At 30% absorbed, flight.air.E is about 0.3% larger than the energy balance allows. Air plus landing come to 1.0030 x Eobj, and the page prints the air taking 8.35 MJ of a baseball that had 8.32 MJ. The ocean figure (decision 10) is inflated by the same factor. This tally is new code; main had none.

findings.title: Several 'their power' labels still appear where the power changed nothing

findings.evidence: Arm wrestle at logKg 2.7085 (511 kg), all-out: 'Held together by their power: the table never breaks' and the tile 'Table carries any force — held together by their power'. With keepForm off: 'Table holds', 'up to 15.1 kN' against a 1.25 kN push. Collide, Rex bolted, set speed 1.19 m/s: chip 'The ground holds: their power'. With the power off: 'Rock around his bolts holds' (gReal is computed but rockChip ignores it). Throw car at 90°: tile 'into the planet: their power', but engine anchor.R is Infinity and v is 30.714 m/s with ownRecoil on and off. Default Wrestle throw (lands at 22.3 m/s, 180 g TNT): 'Landing: Unbreakable footing: the ground under him holds, and nothing breaks'. Powers off: 'Landing: Ollie is indestructible, so the landing is the ground’s problem' (no crater).

verdict.reasoning: Three of the four cases reproduced. Each breaks the brief's 'Page: each power shows where it changed a result'. (a) Arm wrestle at 511 kg: the push is 1.25 kN against a 15.1 kN table, so the table holds without the power, yet the chip says 'Held together by their power: the table never breaks'. (b) Collide, Rex bolted, 1.19 m/s: rockChip reads rock.comic and ignores gReal. It shows 'The ground holds: their power' though the rock holds without it ('Rock around his bolts holds', 6.76 kN). (c) Throw car at 90°: the tile says 'into the planet: their power', but R is Infinity and v is 30.714 m/s with the power on or off. (d) Wrestle landing: reproduced, but weaker. With the power off the page has no landing ground-damage model ('the ground's problem'), so whether the power changed anything there is unknown, not shown to be false.
verdict.reproduction: Arm: node page.js branch '{"state":{"duoOpen":true,"duoAction":"arm","logKg":2.7085},"bay":"duo-bay","duoEffort":"allout"}' -> 'Held together by their power: the table never breaks', tile 'Table carries any force held together by their power'. With keepForm false: 'Table holds', 'Table carries up to 15.1 kN'; arm force 'Rex 1.25 kN, Ollie 1.25 kN'. Collide: {colSrc:'set', colGB:log10(1.19/c), anchor:'bolted'} -> 'The ground holds: their power'; with unbreakable false -> 'Rock around his bolts holds ... load on the rock ... 6.76 kN'. Throw 90°: tile 'His recoil none into the planet: their power'; f10c.js: ownRecoil true R Infinity v 30.71419; ownRecoil false R Infinity v 30.71419 recoilV 0. Wrestle throw default: on 'Landing: Unbreakable footing: the ground under him holds, and nothing breaks; the landing still shakes it.'; off 'Landing: Ollie is indestructible, so the landing is the ground's problem.' (lands at 22.3 m/s, 180 g TNT).
verdict.better_fix: Arm (2148): credit only if P.armWrestle(ctx with keepForm:false, ...) would break the table (tableRatio or slamRatio > 1); otherwise use the plain 'Table holds' chip and the real 'up to 15.1 kN' tile. rockChip: take gReal and use rock.comic && gReal && gReal.broke ? 'The ground holds: their power' : the real rock chip computed from gReal. Throw tile (1466): 'into the planet: their power' only when rOwn0.recoilV > 0.01 or isFinite(rOwn0.anchor.R); otherwise 'push aimed so steeply down his feet can’t slide'. Wrestle landing: drop the Unbreakable footing credit unless a real-ground landing model says it breaks.

findings.outcome: fixed: the arm table credited only when the same bout without Things keep their form breaks it; rockChip uses the real-ground rock; the throw recoil tile credits their power only when the recoil changed; the Wrestle landing credit only when the real landing makes a crater
